topicName: Composite Index Design and Leftmost Prefix Rule
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Composite Index Design and Leftmost Prefix Rule"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"In SQL tuning, understanding how database engines utilize composite indexes is critical for optimizing query performance. A composite index (or multicolumn index) is an index defined on two or more columns of a table."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"The Mechanics of Composite Indexes"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"When you create a composite index on columns (A, B, C), the database sorts the index entries primarily by column A. When column A values are identical, it sorts by column B, and then by column C. This hierarchical sorting is what makes the Leftmost Prefix Rule fundamental."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"The Leftmost Prefix Rule Explained"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Leftmost Prefix Rule states that a composite index can be used by the query optimizer only if the query references the columns from the left side of the index in sequential order without skipping any leading columns."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Index defined on: (col_a, col_b, col_c)"},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Valid query patterns: col_a, (col_a and col_b), or (col_a, col_b, and col_c)"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Invalid prefix skips: (col_b) alone, (col_c) alone, or (col_b and col_c)"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Code Examples for Valid and Invalid Scenarios"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Consider a table named \"orders\" with a composite index on (\"status\", \"customer_id\", \"order_date\"). Review the following SQL statements to see how the optimizer treats different WHERE clauses."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'PENDING' AND customer_id = 1042; -- Uses index (Leftmost prefix honored)"},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'PENDING'; -- Uses index (Leftmost single column honored)"},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 1042; -- Full table scan (Skipped leading 'status' column)"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Composite Index Design"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Place columns used in equality checks (e.g., status = 'ACTIVE') first in the composite index definition."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Place columns used in range queries (e.g., order_date > '2023-01-01') toward the right end of the index."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Audit your workload frequently to drop redundant indexes where a composite index can serve multiple single-column query needs."}]
